source_text: Καὶ ὅτι διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ ὑμῶν καὶ διὰ τὰς εἰδωλολατρείας, ἀλλ᾿ οὐ διὰ τὸ ἐνδεὴς εἶναι τῶν τοιούτων προσφορῶν, ἐνετείλατο ὁμοίως ταῦτα γίνεσθαι, ἀκούσατε πῶς περὶ τούτων λέγει διὰ Ἀμώς, ἑνὸς τῶν δώδεκα, βοῶν· Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐπιθυμοῦντες τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ κυρίου. Ἵνα τί αὕτη ὑμῖν ἡ ἡμέρα κυρίου: Καὶ αὐτή ἐστι σκότος καὶ οὐ φῶς. Ὅν τρόπον ὅταν ἐκφύγῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ λέοντος, καὶ συναντήσῃ αὐτῷ ἡ ἄρκτος, καὶ εἰσπηδήσῃ εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπερείσηται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν τοῖχον, καὶ δάκῃ αὐτὸν ὁ ὄφις. Οὐχὶ σκότος ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου καὶ οὐ φῶς, καὶ γνόφος οὐκ ἔχων φέγγος αὐτῆς; Μεμίσηκα, ἀπῶσμαι τὰς ἑορτὰς ὑμῶν, καὶ οὐ μὴ ὀσφρανθῶ ἐν ταῖς πανηγύρεσιν ὑμῶν. Διότι ἐὰν ἐνέγκητέ μοι τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ τὰς θυσίας ὑμῶν, οὐ προσδέξομαι αὐτὰ καὶ σωτηρίου ἐπιφανείας ὑμῶν οὐκ ἐπιβλέψομαι. Ἀπόστησον ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ πλῆθος ᾠδῶν σου καὶ ψαλμῶν· ὀργάνων σου οὐκ ἀκούσομαι. Καὶ κυλισθήσεται ὡς ὕδωρ κρίμα καὶ ἡ δικαιοσύνη ὡς χειμάρρους ἄβατος. Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ; λέγει κύριος. Καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν Ῥαφάν, τοὺς τύπους, οὓς ἐποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς. Καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Δαμασκοῦ, λέγει κύριος· ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὄνομα αὐτῷ. Οὐαὶ οἱ κατασπαταλῶντες Σιὼν καὶ τοῖς πεποιθόσιν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σαμαρείας. Οἱ ὠνομασμένοι ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀρχηγοῖς ἀπετρύγησαν ἀρχὰς ἐθνῶν· εἰσῆλθον ἑαυτοῖς οἶκος Ἰσραήλ. Διάβητε πάντες εἰς Χαλάνην καὶ ἴδετε, καὶ πορεύθητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Ἀμὰθ τὴν μεγάλην, καὶ κατάβητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Γὲθ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, τὰς κρατίστας ἐκ πασῶν τῶν βασιλειῶν τούτων, εἰ πλείονά ἐστι τὰ ὅρια αὐτῶν τῶν ὁρίων ὑμῶν. Οἱ ἐρχόμενοι εἰς ἡμέραν πονηράν, οἱ ἐγγίζοντες καὶ ἐφαπτόμενοι σαββάτων ψευδῶν, οἱ κοιμώμενοι ἐπὶ κλινῶν ἐλεφαντίνων καὶ κατασπαταλῶντες ἐπὶ ταῖς στρωμναῖς αὐτῶν, οἱ ἐσθίοντες ἄρνας ἐκ ποιμνίων καὶ μοσχάρια ἐκ μέσου βουκολίων γαλαθηνά, οἱ ἐπικροτοῦντες πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τῶν ὀργάνων, ὡς ἑστῶτα ἐλογίσαντο καὶ οὐχ ὡς φεύγοντα, οἱ πίνοντες ἐν φιάλαις οἶνον καὶ τὰ πρῶτα μύρα χριόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ἔπασχον οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῇ συντριβῇ τοῦ Ἰωσήφ. Διὰ τοῦτο νῦν αἰχμάλωτοι ἔσονται ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς δυναστῶν τῶν ἀποικιζομένων, καὶ μεταστραφήσεται οἴκημα κακούργων, καὶ ἐξαρθήσεται χρεμετισμὸς ἵππων ἐξ Ἐφραΐμ . Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ἱερεμίου· Συναγάγετε τὰ κρέα ὑμῶν καὶ τὰς θυσίας καὶ φάγετε, ὅτι οὔτε περὶ θυσιῶν ἢ σπονδῶν ἐνετειλάμην τοῖς πατράσιν ὑμῶν, ῄ ἡμέρᾳ ἐπελαβόμην τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου [JÉR., VII, 21-22]. Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Δαυΐδ ἐν τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ οὕτως ἔφη· Θεὸς θεῶν κύριος ἐλάλησε, καὶ ἐκάλεσε τὴν γῆν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν ἡλίου μέχρι δυσμῶν. Ἐκ Σιὼν ἡ εὐπρέπεια τῆς ὡραιότητος αὐτοῦ. Ὁ θεὸς ἐμφανῶς ἥξει, ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, καὶ οὐ παρασιωπήσεται· πῦρ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ καυθήσεται, καὶ κύκλῳ αὐτοῦ καταιγὶς σφόδρα. Προσκαλέσεται τὸν οὐρανὸν ἂνω καὶ τὴν γῆν τοῦ διακρῖναι τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ. Συναγάγετε αὐτῷ τοὺς ὁσίους αὐτοῦ, τοὺς διατιθεμένους τὴν διαθήκην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ θυσίαις. Καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσιν οἱ οὐρανοὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, ὅτι θεὸς κριτής ἐστιν. Ἄκουσον, λαός μου, καὶ λαλήσω σοι, Ἰσραήλ, καὶ διαμαρτυροῦμαί σοι· ὁ θεός, ὁ θεός σου εἰμὶ ἐγώ. Οὐκ ἐπὶ ταῖς θυσίαις σου ἐλέγξω σε· τὰ δὲ ὁλοκαυτώματά σου ἐνώπιόν μου ἐστὶ διὰ παντός. Οὐ δέξομαι ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου σου μόσχους οὐδὲ ἐκ τῶν ποιμνίων σου χιμάρους, ὅτι ἐμά ἐστι πάντα τὰ θηρία τοῦ ἀγροῦ, κτήνη ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι καὶ βόες· ἔγνωκα πάντα τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ὡραιότης ἀγροῦ μετ᾿ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν. Ἐὰν πεινάσω, οὐ μή σοι εἴπω· ἐμὴ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ οἰκουμένη καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Μὴ φάγωμαι κρέα ταύρων. ἢ αἷμα τράγων πίωμαι; Θῦσον τῷ θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως. καὶ ἀπόδος τῷ ὑψίστῳ τὰς εὐχάς σου· καὶ ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με. Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἵνα τί σὺ ἐκδιηγῇ τὰ δικαιώματά μου, καὶ ἀναλαμβάνεις τὴν διαθήκην μου διὰ στόματός σου; Σὺ δὲ ἐμίσησας παιδείαν καὶ ἐξέβαλες τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω. Εἰ ἐθεώρεις κλέπτην, συνέτρεχες αὐτῷ, καὶ μετὰ μοιχοῦ τὴν μερίδα σου ἐτίθεις. Τὸ στόμα σου ἐπλεόνασε κακίαν, καὶ ἡ γλῶσσά σου περιέπλεκε δολιότητας. Καθήμενος κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου κατελάλεις, καὶ κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς μητρός σου ἐτίθεις σκάνδαλον. Ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα· ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος. Ἐλέγξω σε καὶ παραστήσω κατὰ πρόσωπόν σου τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου. Σύνετε δὴ ταῦτα οἱ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι τοῦ θεοῦ, μήποτε ἁρπάσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ᾖ ὁ ῥυόμενος. Θυσία αἰνέσεως δοξάσει με, καὶ ἐκεὶ ὁδός, ἥν δείξω αὐτῷ τὸ σωτήριόν μου . Οὔτε οὖν θυσίας παρ᾿ ὑμῶν λαμβάνει, οὔτε ὡς ἐνδεὴς τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐνετείλατο ποιεῖν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὑμῶν. Καὶ γὰρ τὸν ναὸν τὸν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπικληθέντα οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεὴς ὢν ὡμολόγησεν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ἢ αὐλήν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅπως καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο προσέχοντες αὐτῷ μὴ εἰδωλολατρῆτε. Καὶ ὅτι τοῦτό ἐστιν, Ἡσαΐας λέγει· Ποῖον οἶκον ᾠκοδομήσατέ μοι; λέγει κύριος. Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, καὶ ἡ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου .
pass_a_gloss: And that because of the sins of your people and because of the idolatries, but not because He is in need of such offerings, He commanded these things to be done, listen how He speaks about these things through Amos, one of the twelve, crying out: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord. Why is this day of the Lord to you? And it is darkness and not light. Just as when a man escapes from the face of a lion, and a bear meets him, and he rushes into his house and leans his hands on the wall, and a snake bites him. Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light, and gloom without its shining? I have hated, I have rejected your festivals, and I will not smell in your gatherings. For if you bring me your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look at the savior of your appearances. Turn away from me the multitude of your songs and psalms; I will not hear your instruments. And justice will roll down like water, and righteousness like an uncontrollable stream. Did you not bring me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness, house of Israel? says the Lord. And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the types which you made for yourselves. And I will exile you beyond Damascus, says the Lord; the all-powerful God is His name. Woe to those who waste away Zion and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria. Those who are named among the leaders have been corrupted by the beginnings of the nations; the house of Israel has entered among them. Pass by all into Chalane and see, and go from there to Amath the great, and go down from there to Geth of the Philistines, the strongest of all these kingdoms, if their borders are greater than your borders. Those who come on an evil day, those who draw near and touch false sabbaths, those who sleep on ivory beds and waste away on their couches, those who eat lambs from the flocks and calves from the midst of the herds, fat ones, those who strike the strings of instruments, as if they were standing and not fleeing, those who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the first myrrh, and they did not suffer anything at the crushing of Joseph. Therefore, now they will be captives from the beginning of the rulers of those being exiled, and the dwelling of the wicked will be overturned, and the neighing of horses will be taken away from Ephraim. And again through Jeremiah: Gather your flesh and your sacrifices and eat, for I did not command your fathers about sacrifices or drink offerings on the day I took their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. And again through David in the forty-ninth psalm he says thus: God of gods, the Lord spoke, and He called the earth from the rising of the sun to the setting. From Zion is the beauty of His goodness. God will come openly, our God, and He will not be silent; fire will burn before Him, and a great storm will be around Him. He will call the heaven above and the earth to judge His people. Gather to Him His holy ones, those who make His covenant through sacrifices. And the heavens will declare His righteousness, for God is a judge. Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, I am. I will not rebuke you for your sacrifices, but your whole burnt offerings are always before me. I will not accept from your house bullocks or from your flocks rams, for all the animals of the field are mine, beasts in the mountains and oxen; I know all the birds of the heaven, and the beauty of the field is with me. If I am hungry, I will not tell you; for the world is mine and its fullness. Will I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God, and pay your vows to the Most High, and call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me. But to the sinner God said: Why do you recite my righteousness and take up my covenant with your mouth? You have hated discipline and cast my words behind you. If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and with an adulterer you placed your portion. Your mouth was full of evil, and your tongue was entwined with deceit. Sitting against your brother you spoke, and against the son of your mother you placed a stumbling block. You did these things, and I was silent; you thought lawlessness, that I will be like you. I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face. Understand these things, you who forget God, lest He seize, and there will be no deliverer. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there I will show him my salvation. He does not receive sacrifices from you, nor did He command to do this because He is in need, but because of your sins. For He did not acknowledge the temple in Jerusalem, called by His name, as His house or court, because He is in need, but so that you, paying attention to this, might not practice idolatry. And that this is so, Isaiah says: What house did you build for me? says the Lord. The heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet.

pass_b_english: The Lord's commands to the people were not because He needed their sacrifices, but because of their sins and idolatries, as He speaks through Amos, one of the twelve prophets, saying, 'Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord - what good will that day be to you? It will be darkness, not light,' (Amos). Just like someone who escapes a lion only to be met by a bear, or who rushes into their house and leans on the wall, only to be bitten by a snake, the day of the Lord will not be a time of joy, but of darkness and gloom, (Amos). The Lord hates and rejects the people's festivals and gatherings, and will not accept their sacrifices or whole burnt offerings, (Amos). He will not look at their appearances or listen to their songs and music, for justice will roll down like water, and righteousness like an uncontrollable stream, (Amos). The Lord asks, 'Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness, house of Israel?' (Amos). The people had taken up the tent of Moloch and the star of their god Rephan, and the Lord says, 'I will exile you beyond Damascus,' (Amos). The Lord also says, 'Woe to those who waste away Zion and trust in the mountain of Samaria,' (Amos). Those who are leaders have been corrupted by the nations, and the house of Israel has followed their example, (Amos). The Lord invites the people to visit the strongest kingdoms and see if their borders are greater than Israel's, (Amos). But those who come on an evil day, who draw near and touch false sabbaths, who sleep on ivory beds and waste away on their couches, eating lambs and calves, and drinking wine, will be captives and their dwelling will be overturned, (Amos). The Lord says through Jeremiah, 'Gather your flesh and your sacrifices and eat, for I did not command your fathers about sacrifices or drink offerings when I led them out of Egypt,' (Jeremiah 7:21-22). The Lord also speaks through David in Psalm 49, saying, 'God, the Lord, spoke and called the earth from the rising of the sun to the setting, and from Zion comes the beauty of His goodness,' (Psalm 49). God will come openly, and fire will burn before Him, and a great storm will be around Him, (Psalm 49). He will call the heaven and the earth to judge His people, and gather His holy ones who make His covenant through sacrifices, (Psalm 49). The heavens will declare His righteousness, for God is a judge, (Psalm 49). The Lord says, 'Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I will testify against you: I am your God,' (Psalm 49). He will not rebuke them for their sacrifices, but their whole burnt offerings are always before Him, (Psalm 49). The Lord says, 'I will not accept bullocks or rams from your house, for all the animals of the field are mine,' (Psalm 49). If He is hungry, He will not tell them, for the world is His and its fullness, (Psalm 49). The Lord says, 'Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to me, and pay your vows to the Most High, and call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me,' (Psalm 49). But to the sinner, God says, 'Why do you recite my righteousness and take up my covenant with your mouth, when you have hated discipline and cast my words behind you?' (Psalm 49). The Lord says, 'I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face, and you will understand that I am not like you,' (Psalm 49). The Lord warns, 'Understand these things, you who forget God, lest He seize, and there will be no deliverer,' (Psalm 49). A sacrifice of praise will glorify the Lord, and He will show His salvation, (Psalm 49). The Lord does not receive sacrifices because He is in need, but because of the people's sins, (Isaiah). He did not acknowledge the temple in Jerusalem as His house or court because He is in need, but so that the people might not practice idolatry, (Isaiah). As Isaiah says, 'What house did you build for me? The heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet,' (Isaiah). The Lord's commands and warnings are clear, and the people must listen and understand, lest they face His judgment and wrath, (Amos, Jeremiah 7:21-22, Psalm 49, Isaiah).

review.notes: Pass B fails on agency and content accuracy. 1. In the section regarding the sinner, Pass B translates 'ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος' as 'you will understand that I am not like you', whereas the Greek and Pass A correctly identify the subject/action: 'you thought lawlessness, that I will be like you' (you assumed lawlessness [would go unpunished], thinking that I would be like you). 2. Pass B adds a concluding summary sentence 'The Lord's commands and warnings are clear...' which is not present in the Greek source. 3. Pass B misattributes the final section regarding the Temple and Isaiah to 'Isaiah' in its parenthetical citations, whereas the Greek text attributes the preceding logic to the context of the argument and then introduces the quote 'Isaiah says'. While the quote is Isaiah, the attribution of the preceding clause 'He did not acknowledge the temple...' to Isaiah is an addition not in the Greek.
reasons: Pass B misrepresents the agency/meaning of 'ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος' by translating it as 'you will understand that I am not like you' instead of 'you thought lawlessness, that I will be like you'; Pass B adds a concluding summary sentence not found in the source; Pass B adds parenthetical citations to the final section that are not explicitly in the Greek text.
